4.61.m: Agastya said:
O six-faced one, I have heard the sin-destroying narrative of Mādhava;
the beneficent majesty of Pañcanada has also been fully heard.
What Mādhava, the slayer of demons, was asked by Agnibindu,
proclaim the answer to that, as it was declared by the foe of Madhu.
Skanda said:
Listen, O great seer Agastya, to what is now being spoken by me,
just as it was recounted by Mādhava to the sage Agnibindu.
Bindumādhava said:
First, know me as Ādikeśava at the Pādodaka sacred ford,
O Agnibindu of great wisdom, the bestower of liberation upon devotees.
Those who worship Ādikeśava in the Avimukta, the immortal sacred field,
truly attain immortality, freed from all sorrow.
Having consecrated the great liṅga Saṅgameśa, Ādikeśava,
destroying sins through mere sight, ever bestows worldly enjoyment and liberation upon men.
South of Pādodaka is the exceedingly great Śvetadvīpa sacred ford;
there I bestow knowledge on men, named Jñānakeśava.
A man, having bathed at Śvetadvīpa in the presence of Jñānakeśava,
never falls away from knowledge on account of worshipping Jñānakeśava.
Bearing the name Tārkṣyakeśava at the Tārkṣya sacred ford, by the best of men

4.61.s: pūjanīyaḥ sadā bhaktyā tārkṣya vatte priyā mama .. 9 ..
4.61.d: पूजनीयः सदा भक्त्या तार्क्ष्य वत्ते प्रिया मम .. 9 ..
4.61.m: I must always be worshipped with devotion; like Garuḍa, they are dear to me.
Right there, at the Nārada sacred ford, I am Nāradakeśava,
and the teacher of the knowledge of Brahman for those whose bodies have bathed in that sacred ford.
Right there is the Prahlāda sacred ford; known by the name Prahlādakeśava,
I should be worshipped by devotees for the abundance of great devotion.
There, at the Ambarīṣa sacred ford, by name indeed Ādityakeśava,
I destroy the mass of darkness of sins even in an instant.
South of Dattātreyeśvara, I am Ādigadādhara;
there I remove the multitude of diseases of saṃsāra for devotees.
Right there, at the Bhārgava sacred ford, by the name Bhṛgukeśava,
I fulfill with desires a man residing in Kāśī.
At the great, auspicious sacred ford named Vāmana, which grants the heart's desire,
I am to be worshipped by those desiring welfare under the name Vāmanakeśava.
At the Naranārāyaṇa tīrtha, [worshipping me] who am embodied as Naranārāyaṇa,
devotees having worshipped me certainly become one with Naranārāyaṇa.
At the sacred ford called Yajñavarāha, [known] by the name Yajñavārāha,
I am to be worshipped by men seeking the fruit of all sacrifices.
I am Vidāranarasiṃha, tearer of obstacles in Kāśī;
I am to be served at the sacred ford bearing that name for the pacification of afflictions at the tīrtha.
At the Gopīgovinda tīrtha, having worshipped me

4.61.s: samarcya māṃ naro bhaktyā mama māyāṃ na saṃspṛśet.. 19 ..
4.61.d: समर्च्य मां नरो भक्त्या मम मायां न संस्पृशेत्.. 19 ..
4.61.m: known by the name Gopīgovinda with devotion, a man shall not be touched by my illusion.
O sage, I am Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha at the pure sacred ford bearing that name;
I bestow glorious fortune upon those endowed with devotion through perpetual gifts.
Bearing the name Śeṣamādhava at the sin-destroying Śeṣa tīrtha,
I grant all special desires contemplated by devotees without remainder.
And having bathed at the Śaṅkhamādhava tīrtha, having bathed me, Śaṅkhamādhava,
with conch-water, one becomes master of the treasure of the conch.
At the great sacred ford of Hayagrīva, having bowed to me,
Hayagrīvakeśava, one will surely attain that supreme abode of Viṣṇu.
I am named Bhīṣmakeśava to the west of Vṛddhakāleśa;
served with devotion, I remove terrible afflictions.
And I am Nirvāṇakeśava, indicating liberation to devotees;
in the northern region from Lolārka, I remove the fickleness of the mind.
Adored to the south of Trailokyasundarī, he who worships me

4.61.s: kāśyāṃ khyātaṃ tribhuvanakeśavaṃ na sa garbhabhāk .. 26 ..
4.61.d: काश्यां ख्यातं त्रिभुवनकेशवं न स गर्भभाक् .. 26 ..
4.61.m: famed in Kāśī as Tribhuvanakeśava does not enter a womb [again].
Know me as Jñānamādhava before the Jñānavāpī;

4.61.s: tatra māṃ bhaktitobhyarcya jñānaṃ prāpnoti śāśvatam .. 27 ..
4.61.d: तत्र मां भक्तितोभ्यर्च्य ज्ञानं प्राप्नोति शाश्वतम् .. 27 ..
4.61.m: having worshipped me there with devotion, one attains eternal knowledge.
Named Śvetamādhava near Viśālākṣī,
worshipped with devotion, I shall produce the form of the lord of Śvetadvīpa.
North of Daśāśvamedha, [seeing] me, Mādhava named Prayāga,
having bathed properly in the Prayāga tīrtha, having seen [me], one is freed from sins.
Whatever fruit is heard [to arise] in the month of Tapas for men who go to Prayāga,
tenfold that fruit arises having bathed here before me.
Whatever merit belongs to those performing ablutions at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and Yamunā,
ten times greater is that merit here in Kāśī in my presence.
Whatever fruit belongs to those giving gifts when the sun is seized by Rāhu
at Kurukṣetra, tenfold greater is that right here in Kāśī.
Where the Gaṅgā flows northward and the Yamunā flows eastward,
having reached their confluence, a man is freed from the slaying of a brahmin.

4.61.s: vapanaṃ tatra kartavyaṃ piṃḍadānaṃ ca bhāvataḥ ..
4.61.d: वपनं तत्र कर्तव्यं पिंडदानं च भावतः ..
4.61.m: Shaving is to be done there, and the offering of rice-balls with devout feeling;
gifts are to be given there by one desiring great fruit.
All the virtues that are proclaimed in the sacred field of Prajāpati
are indeed innumerable in the great sacred field Avimukta.
The great liṅga Prayāgeśa stands there granting desires;
and by its presence that sacred ford is proclaimed wish-fulfilling.

4.61.s: kāśyāṃ māghaḥ prayāge yairna snāto makarārkagaḥ ..
4.61.d: काश्यां माघः प्रयागे यैर्न स्नातो मकरार्कगः ..
4.61.m: Those by whom the month of Māgha with the sun in Capricorn was not bathed at Prayāga in Kāśī
at the break of dawn—whence their ultimate bliss?

4.61.s: kāśyudbhave prayāge ye tapasi snāṃti saṃyatāḥ ..
4.61.d: काश्युद्भवे प्रयागे ये तपसि स्नांति संयताः ..
4.61.m: Those who, self-restrained, bathe in the month of Tapas at the Prayāga arising in Kāśī,
the fruit produced by the ten horse-sacrifices is surely theirs.
Those who, having bathed at Prayāga in the month of Tapas, always worship daily
Prayāgamādhava and Prayāgeśa, granter of desires, with devotion,
having obtained wealth, grain, prosperity of sons, and delightful pleasures,
having enjoyed supreme bliss here, attain supreme liberation.
Indeed, in the month of Māgha all sacred fords go together to Prayāga
from the east, north, west, south, below, and above.

4.61.s: kāśīsthitāni tīrthāni mune yāṃti na kutracit ..

4.61.m: The sacred fords located in Kāśī, O sage, go nowhere;
if they go, they go to the unsurpassed triad of sacred fords.
In the month of Ūrja, they come to Pañcanada every morning near me,
which calms the great flood of sins and bestows supreme welfare.
Having reached the month of Māgha, the enemy of sins, near Prayāgeśa,
in the morning at Prayāga all the sacred fords bathe following me;
and having reached midday, they constantly depart.
All the sacred fords [come] to bathe completely in Maṇikarṇikā, which bestows liberation. // 45
This supreme secret regarding Kāśī has been told to you, O sage,
showing how the triad of sacred fords is superior, particularly each at its own proper time. // 46
I shall tell another secret that must not be spoken anywhere [at random];

4.61.s: abhakteṣu sadā gopyaṃ na gopyaṃ bhaktimajjane .. 47 ..
4.61.d: अभक्तेषु सदा गोप्यं न गोप्यं भक्तिमज्जने .. 47 ..
4.61.m: it must always be concealed from non-devotees, but not concealed from a devoted person. // 47
All the sacred fords in Kāśī, each progressively greater than the other,
surely destroy great sins forcibly by their own spiritual power. // 48
This very secret of Vārāṇasī is declared to you
with a raised finger as the truth: Maṇikarṇikā alone is supreme. // 49
All the sacred fords, situated in their respective domains, roar, ah,
solely upon attaining the exceedingly great power belonging to Maṇikarṇikā. // 4.2.61.50
Having destroyed the sins of sinners, even great and numerous ones,
the sacred fords of Kāśī at midday, desiring to perform expiation,
on festival days or even on non-festival days, constantly observing vows, ah,
surely become immaculate by plunging into Maṇikarṇikā. // 52
The Lord of the Universe (Viśveśa), together with the Lady of the Universe, always near Maṇikarṇikā,
having arrived at midday, performs his ritual ablution every single day. // 53
Even from Vaikuṇṭha, I too constantly, at midday, into Maṇikarṇikā

4.61.s: vigāhe padmayā sārdhaṃ mudā paramayā mune .. 54 ..
4.61.d: विगाहे पद्मया सार्धं मुदा परमया मुने .. 54 ..
4.61.m: plunge together with Padmā in supreme joy, O sage. // 54
That I take away the sins of those who utter my name even once,
having obtained the name 'Hari', is by virtue of that power of Maṇikarṇikā. // 55
From Satyaloka every day, the Grandfather [Brahmā], who rides a swan,
comes to Maṇikarṇikā to perform the midday rites. // 56
Indra and the other world-protectors, and the great seers headed by Marīci,
gather at Maṇikarṇikā to perform the midday rites. // 57
And the serpents headed by Śeṣa and Vāsuki, from the realm of the serpents,
come here at midday to bathe in Maṇikarṇikā. // 58
Among all things moving and unmoving, as many conscious beings as there are,
that many bathe at midday in the pure water of Maṇikarṇikā. // 59
Who are able to describe the exceedingly weighty virtues of Maṇikarṇikā,
O brahmins, innumerable even by myself and others? // 4.2.61.60
Fierce austerities were performed in the forests by those whose wealth is austerity,
by whom this Maṇikarṇikā, the realm of liberation, was indeed reached. // 61
They alone are bulls among men who have distributed great gifts,
by whom this Maṇikarṇikā was reached in the final stage of life. // 62
They have indeed performed all vows according to the prescribed rule,
by whom the soft ground of Maṇikarṇikā has been made their bed. // 63
They alone among mortals are fortunate, consecrated in all sacrifices,
by whom, having abandoned wealth earned through merit, Maṇikarṇikā was beheld. // 64
Various religious duties, both sacrificial and charitable, were performed by those men
by whom Maṇikarṇikā was reached upon arriving at old age. // 65
Gems, fine silken garments, gold, elephants, and horses
should be given by a wise man with diligence always near Maṇikarṇikā. // 66
Wealth earned by merit, even if very little, which is given by men,
that is eternally inexhaustible, O sage, at Maṇikarṇikā. // 67
If the best of men performs even a single breath-control as prescribed,

4.61.s: yastena vihito nūnaṃ ṣaḍaṃgo yoga uttamaḥ .. 68 ..
4.61.d: यस्तेन विहितो नूनं षडंगो योग उत्तमः .. 68 ..
4.61.m: by him the supreme six-limbed yoga has surely been performed. // 68
Having recited even a single Gāyatrī after reaching Maṇikarṇikā,
one clearly obtains the fruit of chanting ten thousand Gāyatrīs. // 69
Having offered even a single oblation near Maṇikarṇikā, the wise man
shall obtain the undiminished fruit of a lifelong Agnihotra. // 4.2.61.70
Having heard this speech of Hari, Agnibindu of great austerity,
bowing down with great devotion, asked Mādhava once more: // 71
Agnibindu said:
O Viṣṇu, what is the extent of this holy Maṇikarṇikā?
Tell me, O lotus-eyed one; there is no other knower of truth than you. // 72
Śrī Viṣṇu said:
From Gaṅgākeśava up to the pavilion of Hariścandra,
and from the middle of the celestial river to Svardvāra is Maṇikarṇikā. // 73
This is the gross extent; and now I shall tell you the subtle [extent]:
In front of the sacred ford of Hariścandra is Hariścandra-Vināyaka,
and here, to the north of the pool of Maṇikarṇikā, is Sīmā-Vināyaka.
A best of men who worships Sīmā-Vināyaka with devotion,
with sweet modaka dumplings and proper offerings, will reach Maṇikarṇikā.
They should offer tarpaṇa to the ancestors at the great sacred ford of Hariścandra;

4.61.s: śataṃ samāḥsu tṛptāḥ syuḥ prayacchaṃti ca vāṃcchitam..
4.61.d: शतं समाःसु तृप्ताः स्युः प्रयच्छंति च वांच्छितम्..
4.61.m: the ancestors will remain satisfied for a hundred years and grant what is desired.
Having bathed at the great sacred ford of Hariścandra, a person endowed with faith
and bowing to Hariścandreśvara does not fall away from truth.
Then there is Parvatatīrtha, near Parvateśvara,
the site of Mahāmeru, destroying heinous sins.
Having bathed there, worshipped the Lord, and given a little according to one's means,
one ascends the peak of Meru and enjoys divine delights.
The sacred ford Kambalāśvatara is to the south of Parvateśvara,
and auspicious Kambalāśvatareśa is to the west of that sacred ford.
Whoever takes a ritual bath in that sacred ford and thoroughly worships that liṅga,

4.61.s: api tasya kule jātā gītajñāḥ syuḥ śriyānvitāḥ ..
4.61.d: अपि तस्य कुले जाता गीतज्ञाः स्युः श्रियान्विताः ..
4.61.m: even those born in their lineage will be skilled in singing and endowed with prosperity.
There is Cakrapuṣkariṇī, which averts the cycle of wombs;
having bathed there, a person does not enter the dense cycle of worldly existence.
Cakrapuṣkariṇī-tīrtha is my supreme abode;
there great austerity was practiced by me for years numbering half a parārdha.

4.61.s: tatra pratyakṣatāṃ yāto mama viśveśvaraḥ paraḥ .. 84..
4.61.d: तत्र प्रत्यक्षतां यातो मम विश्वेश्वरः परः .. 84..
4.61.m: There Viśveśvara, the supreme Lord, became visible before my eyes;
there I obtained imperishable, greatest sovereignty.
And Cakrapuṣkariṇī became renowned as Maṇikarṇikā;
giving up her liquid form, she assumed the form of a woman,
and Maṇikarṇikā was beheld there by me in visible form.

4.61.s: tasyā rūpaṃ pravakṣyāmi bhaktānāṃ śubhadaṃ param ..
4.61.d: तस्या रूपं प्रवक्ष्यामि भक्तानां शुभदं परम् ..
4.61.m: I shall describe her form, which grants the highest good to devotees,
by meditating on whose form at the three junctures of day for six months
the goddess Maṇikarṇikā is seen by men in visible form:
Four-armed, large-eyed, with a glittering eye on her forehead,
ever facing the west, with her hands folded together,
holding a garland of blue lotuses in her right hand,

4.61.s: varodyate kare savye mātuluṃga phalaṃ śubham ..
4.61.d: वरोद्यते करे सव्ये मातुलुंग फलं शुभम् ..
4.61.m: and in her left hand raised in granting boons, an auspicious citron fruit.
Ever having the form of a maiden, ever twelve years of age,
with the luster of pure crystal, and dark-blue, glossy hair,
with delightful lips that surpass coral and rubies,
her head adorned with a hair-bun radiant with fresh ketakī flowers,
with pearl ornaments on all her limbs, covered in a garment with the luster of the moon,
bearing on her bosom a splendid garland made of white lotuses.
In this form she is to be meditated upon day and night by those who seek liberation—
glorious Maṇikarṇikā, the abode of the fortune of nirvāṇa.
And I will proclaim her mantra, named 'Wish-fulfilling Tree of Devotees,'
by whose repetition even the eight supernatural perfections are achieved by men:
One should first utter the seed-syllables of speech, māyā, lakṣmī, love, and praṇava [aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ oṃ];
then the word maṇi, then the word ending in bhā with bindu [bhaṃ], then karṇike, enveloped with hṛd [namaḥ] and praṇava [oṃ].
This mantra, equal to the tree of the gods, bestowing a succession of all happiness, is to be recited;
having letters measured by fifteen, it grants the supreme state to those of sharp intellect.
The praṇava [oṃ], the third from the praṇava [aim], ending in bindu [iṃ], then the word maṇi, then karṇike,
the word ending in praṇava [oṃ], then kena, then ma: such is the mantra whose syllables number fourteen [or fourteen Manus].
This mantra should be recited day and night by men seeking liberation;
a fire-offering of one-tenth [the count] should be performed by men firm in faith and respect,
with unblemished white lotuses bathed in ghee from cow's milk,
mixed with sugar and with honey, the wise person remaining ever pure.
By reciting the mantra three hundred thousand times, even if one dies in other lands,
one certainly attains liberation through the power of this mantra.
A golden image should be made, endowed with the nine gems,
possessing the form described previously, and should be worshipped with diligence.
Or it may be constantly worshipped at home by men longing solely for liberation,
or, having worshipped it diligently, it should then be cast into Maṇikarṇikā.
By men who fear the cycle of rebirth, who are firm in faith and respect here,
this means should be practiced, even by those residing far away.
Having taken a ritual ablution in the Maṇikarṇī [pool], from seeing Maṇikarṇīśa
a man shall not obtain dwelling in the chamber of a mother's womb. // 4
The Maṇikarṇīśvara liṅga was installed of old by me
at the eastern gate of the Antargṛha here; it should be worshipped by those desiring liberation. // 5
Then there is the Pāśupata tīrtha, to the south of Maṇikarṇikā;
having performed the water-rites there, one should behold Paśupatīśvara, // 6
where the Pāśupata yoga was taught by the wielder of the Pināka bow,
which removes the beast-fetters even of myself and the gods headed by Brahmā. // 7
Therefore, where Paśupati himself has assumed the form of a liṅga,
he shines constantly in Kāśī for the release from the beast-fetters. // 8
There, on the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight of Caitra, by those of pure mind,

4.61.s: kāryā yātrā prayatnena rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ tathā .. 9 ..
4.61.d: कार्या यात्रा प्रयत्नेन रात्रौ जागरणं तथा .. 9 ..
4.61.m: a pilgrimage should be made with effort, and likewise a vigil at night. // 9
Having worshipped Paśupati, intent on fasting,
they are not bound by the beast-fetters, having performed the breaking of the fast on the new moon. // 4.2.61.110
Then there is the Rudrāvāsa tīrtha, ahead of the Pāśupata tīrtha;
having bathed there, Hara, the Lord of Rudrāvāsa, should be worshipped by men. // 11
To the south of Maṇikarṇīśvara, a man having worshipped
Rudrāvāseśvara, shall dwell in the realm of Rudrāvāsa; there is no doubt. // 12
Then, to the south, is the Viśva tīrtha, presided over by all sacred fords;

4.61.s: tatra snātvā naro bhaktyā viśvanāthaṃ vilokayet .. 13 ..
4.61.d: तत्र स्नात्वा नरो भक्त्या विश्वनाथं विलोकयेत् .. 13 ..
4.61.m: having bathed there, a man should behold Viśvanātha with devotion. // 13

4.61.s: viśvāṃ gaurīṃ ca tadanu pūjayitvāti bhaktitaḥ ..
4.61.d: विश्वां गौरीं च तदनु पूजयित्वाति भक्तितः ..
4.61.m: And after that, having worshipped Viśvā Gaurī with intense devotion,

4.61.s: viśvasya pūjyo bhavati tato viśvamayo bhavet .. 14 ..
4.61.d: विश्वस्य पूज्यो भवति ततो विश्वमयो भवेत् .. 14 ..
4.61.m: he becomes worthy of worship by the universe, and then he becomes identical with the universe. // 14
And after that is the Mukti tīrtha; having bathed there as well,
and then having worshipped Mokṣeśvara, he attains liberation without doubt. // 15
Having beheld Mokṣeśa to the west of Avimukteśvara,
a human being does not make coming and going in the human world again, ah! // 16
The Avimukteśvara tīrtha is just beyond the Mukti tīrtha;
having bathed there and worshipped Avimukteśa, one is fully liberated. // 17

4.61.s: tatpare tārakaṃ tīrthaṃ yatra viśveśvaraḥ svayam ..
4.61.d: तत्परे तारकं तीर्थं यत्र विश्वेश्वरः स्वयम् ..
4.61.m: Beyond that is the Tāraka tīrtha, where Viśveśvara himself
reveals the Tāraka-Brahman, which is of the nature of immortality, in the ear of the dying. // 18
Having bathed well in the Tāraka tīrtha, from the darśana of Tārakeśvara,
having crossed the ocean of worldly existence, he delivers his ancestors as well. // 19
Near that is the Skanda tīrtha; having bathed there, the best of men,
and having beheld the six-faced one, sheds the body made of the six sheaths. // 4.2.61.120
Having beheld the god, the six-faced one, to the east of Tārakeśvara,
he shall dwell in the world of the six-faced one, bearing a youthful body. // 21
Then there is the sacred Ḍhuṇḍhi tīrtha; a man, having performed water-rites there,
and having praised Ḍhuṇḍhi Gaṇapati, is not overcome by obstacles. // 22
To the south of the Ḍhuṇḍhi tīrtha is the peerless Bhavānī tīrtha;

4.61.s: tatra snātvā vidhānena bhavānīṃ paripūjya ca .. 23..
4.61.d: तत्र स्नात्वा विधानेन भवानीं परिपूज्य च .. 23..
4.61.m: having bathed there according to rule and having worshipped Bhavānī
with fine silk garments, jewel ornaments, and food offerings of great variety,

4.61.s: puṣpairdhūpaiḥ pradīpaiśca bhavānī śo prapūjya ca .. 54 ..
4.61.d: पुष्पैर्धूपैः प्रदीपैश्च भवानी शो प्रपूज्य च .. 54 ..
4.61.m: with flowers, incenses, and lamps, and having worshipped the Lord of Bhavānī,
by him the entire triple world, with the moving and the unmoving, has been worshipped.

one hundred and eight circumambulations should be performed. // 26
By him has been circumambulated the earth containing seven continents,

4.61.s: saśailā sasamudrā ca sāśramā ca sakānanā .. 27 ..
4.61.d: सशैला ससमुद्रा च साश्रमा च सकानना .. 27 ..
4.61.m: together with mountains, together with oceans, together with hermitages, and together with forests. // 27
Eight circumambulations should be offered daily by those intent on contentment;
Bhavānī and Śaṃkara should always be bowed down to with effort. // 28

4.61.s: bhaktānāṃ kāmadā nityaṃ bhavānī vāsasāṃ pradā ..
4.61.d: भक्तानां कामदा नित्यं भवानी वाससां प्रदा ..
4.61.m: Bhavānī constantly grants desires to devotees and provides garments;
therefore, Bhavānī should be worshipped in Kāśī by the dwellers of the sacred ford. // 29
Bhavānī always provides acquisition and preservation of property for the dwellers of Kāśī;
therefore, Bhavānī should be constantly served by the dwellers of Kāśī. // 4.2.61.130
Alms should always be begged by a mendicant desiring liberation,
since in Kāśī, the giver of alms is the housewife of the Lord of the Universe. // 31
In the midst of the home here is the Lord of the Universe, and Bhavānī is his housewife;
to all who reside in Kāśī, she gives the alms of liberation. // 32
Whatever is difficult to obtain for the dwellers of the Kāśī kṣetra,
Bhavānī, when worshipped by men, makes that very easy to obtain. // 33
A person observing a vow should keep a night vigil on the great eighth day [of the lunar fortnight];
having worshipped Bhavānī in the morning, he will obtain his desired fruit. (34)
Whoever gazes upon Bhavānī to the west of Śukreśa,

4.61.s: sarve manorathāstasya siddhyaṃtīha na saṃ śayaḥ .. 35 ..
4.61.d: सर्वे मनोरथास्तस्य सिद्ध्यंतीह न सं शयः .. 35 ..
4.61.m: all his wishes are fulfilled in this world; of this there is no doubt. (35)
One should dwell constantly in Kāśī; one should bathe where [the river] flows north;
Bhavānī and Śaṃkara should be worshipped; enjoyment and liberation are to be attained. (36)

4.61.s: mātarbhavāni tava pādarajobhavāni mātarbhavāni tavadāsataro bhavāni ..
4.61.d: मातर्भवानि तव पादरजोभवानि मातर्भवानि तवदासतरो भवानि ..
4.61.m: “O Mother Bhavānī, may I be the dust of your feet! O Mother Bhavānī, may I be your humble servant!
O Mother Bhavānī, so that I may not be [reborn] in this worldly existence, may I daily belong to you, O Bhavānī, and may I not be born again!” (37)

4.61.s: tiṣṭhatā gacchatā vāpi svapatā jāgratāpi vā ..
4.61.d: तिष्ठता गच्छता वापि स्वपता जाग्रतापि वा ..
4.61.m: Whether standing or walking, sleeping or waking,
this [verse] should constantly be recited here by a resident of Kāśī for the attainment of happiness. (38)
Right there is Īśānatīrtha, in the vicinity of Bhavānītīrtha;

4.61.s: tatra snāto ya īśānamarcayenna sa janmabhāk .. 39 ..
4.61.d: तत्र स्नातो य ईशानमर्चयेन्न स जन्मभाक् .. 39 ..
4.61.m: having bathed there, whoever worships Īśāna is not subject to [further] rebirth. (39)

4.61.s: jñānatīrthaṃ ca tatraiva jñānadaṃ savardā nṛṇām ..
4.61.d: ज्ञानतीर्थं च तत्रैव ज्ञानदं सवर्दा नृणाम् ..
4.61.m: Right there is also Jñānatīrtha, ever the giver of wisdom to men;
having performed an ablution in that sacred ford and beheld the benevolent Jñāneśvara, (40)
[and] by whom Jñāneśa situated near the Jñānavāpī is worshipped,
they will suffer no loss of wisdom, even when approaching death. (41)
Right there is Śailāditīrtha, which reveals the supreme prosperity;

4.61.s: tatra śrāddhādikaṃ kṛtvā dattvā dānaṃ svaśaktitaḥ .. 42 ..
4.61.d: तत्र श्राद्धादिकं कृत्वा दत्त्वा दानं स्वशक्तितः .. 42 ..
4.61.m: having performed an ancestral rite and the like there, and given gifts according to one's means, (42)
[and] beholding Śailādīśvara to the north of the Jñānavāpī,
one attains the station of being a gaṇa; on this no doubt should be entertained. (43)
South of Nanditīrtha, however, is my supreme Viṣṇutīrtha;
offering rice-balls there, one becomes free of debt to the ancestors. (44)

4.61.s: viṣṇutīrthe kṛtasnāno yo māṃ viṣṇuṃ vilokayet ..
4.61.d: विष्णुतीर्थे कृतस्नानो यो मां विष्णुं विलोकयेत् ..
4.61.m: Having bathed at Viṣṇutīrtha, whoever gazes upon me, Viṣṇu,
on the southern side of Viśveśa, goes to the world of Viṣṇu. (45)

4.61.s: yaḥ pratyekādaśīṃ prāpya śayanīṃ bodhinīṃ tathā ..
4.61.d: यः प्रत्येकादशीं प्राप्य शयनीं बोधिनीं तथा ..
4.61.m: Whoever, on every eleventh lunar day, as well as on Śayanī and Bodhinī,
keeps a night vigil near my image, (46)

4.61.s: prātaḥ samarcya māṃ bhaktyā bhojayitvā dvijānapi ..
4.61.d: प्रातः समर्च्य मां भक्त्या भोजयित्वा द्विजानपि ..
4.61.m: having worshipped me with devotion in the morning and fed the twice-born,

4.61.s: dattvā gāḥ kāṃcanaṃ bhūmiṃ na bhūyo bhūmibhāgbhavet ..47..
4.61.d: दत्त्वा गाः कांचनं भूमिं न भूयो भूमिभाग्भवेत् ..47..
4.61.m: and given cows, gold, and land, will not be born again upon the earth. (47)
Having concluded the vow there, free from stinginess regarding wealth,
the wise man truly attains the full fruit of the vow by my command. (48)

4.61.s: mama tīrthādavācyāṃ tu tī rthaṃ paitāmahaṃ śubham ..
4.61.d: मम तीर्थादवाच्यां तु ती र्थं पैतामहं शुभम् ..
4.61.m: South of my sacred ford is the auspicious sacred ford of the Grandfather [Brahmā];
having gratified the grandfathers there through the prescribed rites of the ancestral offering, (49)
and having worshipped with devotion the liṅga Pitāmaheśvara
situated above the Brahmanāla, a person attains the world of Brahmā. (50)

4.61.s: brahmasrotaḥ samīpe tu kṛtaṃ karma śubhāśubham ..
4.61.d: ब्रह्मस्रोतः समीपे तु कृतं कर्म शुभाशुभम् ..
4.61.m: Any deed, auspicious or inauspicious, performed near the Brahmasrotas
attains supreme imperishability; therefore, one should perform only good deeds. (51)
Whatever deed, even the very slightest, is performed here, whether auspicious or inauspicious,
has no destruction even at the cosmic dissolution, O best of sages. (52)
This is declared to be Nābhitīrtha, because it is the navel of the earth;
it is also the navel of the cosmic egg, bringing auspicious prosperity. (53)
This Māṇikarṇikā is that navel, the ground of profound depth,
in which the entire cosmic egg undergoes dissolution and arising. (54)

4.61.s: brahmanālaṃ paraṃ tīrthaṃ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam ..
4.61.d: ब्रह्मनालं परं तीर्थं त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम् ..
4.61.m: Brahmanāla is a supreme sacred ford, renowned throughout the three worlds;

4.61.s: tatsaṃgame naraḥ snātvā koṭijanma malaṃ haret .. 55 ..
4.61.d: तत्संगमे नरः स्नात्वा कोटिजन्म मलं हरेत् .. 55 ..
4.61.m: bathing at its confluence, a person removes the impurity of ten million births. (55)
If even a mere bone belonging to anyone should fall into the Brahmanāla,
they never enter inside the pavilion of the cosmic egg [again]. (56)
Then there is the sacred ford of Bhagīratha, south of Brahmanāla;
having bathed there, a person is completely freed from the murder of a brahmin. (57)
Near Svargadvāra is the liṅga Bhāgīrathīśvara;
from its darśana, the preparatory rite for expiating the murder of a brahmin is said to be accomplished. (58)
A person whose paternal ancestors have met with an unfortunate fate
should diligently offer water libations to them at the Bhāgīrathītīrtha. (59)

4.61.s: tatra bhāgīrathe tīrthe śrāddhaṃ kṛtvā vidhānataḥ ..
4.61.d: तत्र भागीरथे तीर्थे श्राद्धं कृत्वा विधानतः ..
4.61.m: Having performed an ancestral rite according to rule at that sacred ford of Bhagīratha
and fed brahmins, he leads his ancestors to the world of Brahmā. (60)
To the south of that is the great sacred ford called Khurakartarī;
because the ground there was made uneven by the millions of hooves
of the cows that came from Goloka, it is therefore called Khurakartarī. (61–62ab)
Having bathed in that sacred ford, and having performed the rite of rice-balls and water libation, (62cd)
and having beheld the liṅga Khurakartarīśa, one attains Goloka;
by worshiping that liṅga, one is never deprived of the wealth of cattle. (63)
To the south of Khurakartarī is the excellent Mārkaṇḍa sacred ford.
Having performed the rites of śrāddha in that sin-destroying sacred ford,
and beholding the liṅga Mārkaṇḍeyeśvara, one attains a long life,

4.61.s: brahmatejobhivṛddhiṃ ca kīrtiṃ ca paramāṃ bhuvi .. 65 ..
4.61.d: ब्रह्मतेजोभिवृद्धिं च कीर्तिं च परमां भुवि .. 65 ..
4.61.m: an increase in brahminical radiance, and supreme renown on earth.
The supreme Vasiṣṭha sacred ford destroys great sins.
Offering libations to the ancestors there and beholding Vasiṣṭheśa,
a man is not tainted by sins accumulated over three births;
he dwells in the world of Vasiṣṭha, endowed with brahminical radiance.
Right there is the Arundhatī sacred ford, which promotes good fortune for women.
Faithful wives especially should bathe in that sacred ford.
The fault arising from infidelity, by plunging into that sacred ford,
goes to destruction in an instant through the power of Arundhatī.
East of Mārkaṇḍeyeśvara, from the worship of Vasiṣṭheśvara,
a mortal becomes sinless and attains great religious merit.
The forms of Vasiṣṭha and Arundhatī should be diligently worshipped there;

4.61.s: na strī vaidhavyamāpnoti na pumānstrī viyogitām ..71..
4.61.d: न स्त्री वैधव्यमाप्नोति न पुमान्स्त्री वियोगिताम् ..71..
4.61.m: no woman suffers widowhood, and no man suffers separation from his wife.
South of the Vasiṣṭha sacred ford is the excellent Narmadā sacred ford.
Having performed a śrāddha and beholding Narmadeśa,
a wise person, having given a great gift there, is released from the cycle of rebirth.
Then indeed is the Trisaṃdhya sacred ford, east of Trisaṃdhyeśvara.

4.61.s: tatra tīrthe naraḥ snātvā kṛtvā saṃdhyāṃ vidhānataḥ ..
4.61.d: तत्र तीर्थे नरः स्नात्वा कृत्वा संध्यां विधानतः ..
4.61.m: Having bathed in that sacred ford and properly performed twilight devotion,
a man is not overwhelmed by sins arising from the omission of the twilight prayer.
Having beheld Trisaṃdhyeśvara and performed twilight devotion at the three junctures of the day,
a twice-born man attains through faith the merit born of reciting the three Vedas.
Next is the Yoginī sacred ford; a man who has bathed there,
having seen the seat of the Yoginīs, attains yogic perfection.
There is the Agasti sacred ford, which destroys hosts of great sins.
Having bathed there with effort and seen the all-pervading Agastīśvara,

4.61.s: agastikuṃḍe ca tataḥ saṃtarpya ca pitāmahān ..
4.61.d: अगस्तिकुंडे च ततः संतर्प्य च पितामहान् ..
4.61.m: and then having gratified the grandfathers at Agastikuṇḍa,

4.61.s: agastinā sametāṃ ca lopāmudrāṃ praṇamya ca .. 78 ...
4.61.d: अगस्तिना समेतां च लोपामुद्रां प्रणम्य च .. 78 ...
4.61.m: and bowed to Lopāmudrā together with Agasti,
freed from all sins, completely devoid of all afflictions,
that best of men goes together with his ancestors to the world of Śiva.
And south of the Agastya sacred ford is a most purifying sacred ford,
named Gaṅgākeśava, which destroys all sins.

4.61.s: tatra me śubhadāṃ mūrtiṃ mune tattīrthasaṃjñikām ..
4.61.d: तत्र मे शुभदां मूर्तिं मुने तत्तीर्थसंज्ञिकाम् ..
4.61.m: There, O sage, having worshipped with faith my auspicious image named after that sacred ford,
the wise person is glorified in my world.
Having offered rice balls there and given gifts according to one's capacity,
one secures satisfaction for the ancestors lasting a hundred years.
This great extent of Maṇikarṇī has been declared to you,
south from Sīmāvināyaka, destroying all obstacles.
To the east of Vairocanēśvara, I am Vaikuṇṭhamādhava.
Having worshipped me there with devotion, one attains the worship of Vaikuṇṭha.
I am named Vīramādhava, O sage, to the west of Vīreśa;

4.61.s: tatra vratī samabhyarcya na yāmīṃ yātanāṃ labhet .. 85 ..
4.61.d: तत्र व्रती समभ्यर्च्य न यामीं यातनां लभेत् .. 85 ..
4.61.m: having worshipped [me] there, one who keeps vows does not experience torment inflicted by Yama.
I am named Kālamādhava in the presence of Kālabhairava.
Neither the Kali age nor Death can affect my devotee; this is certain.
Fasting on the eleventh day of the bright half of Mārgaśīrṣa,
and keeping a vigil there, one never beholds Yama.
I am Nirvāṇanarasiṃha to the south of Pulastīśvara;
merely by bowing to that image, a devotee attains liberation.
I am Mahābalanṛsiṃha to the east of Oṃkāra, O sage;
one who worships him does not see the mighty messengers of Yama.

4.61.s:
pracaṃḍanarasiṃhohaṃ caṃḍabhairavapūrvataḥ .
pracaṃḍamapyaghaṃ kṛtvā niṣpāpmā syāttadarcanāt .. 4.2.61.190 ..
4.61.d:
प्रचंडनरसिंहोहं चंडभैरवपूर्वतः .
प्रचंडमप्यघं कृत्वा निष्पाप्मा स्यात्तदर्चनात् .. 4.2.61.190 ..
4.61.m: I am Pracaṇḍanarasiṃha to the east of Caṇḍabhairava; / even after committing a fierce sin, one becomes sinless by worshipping him.
I am Girinṛsiṃha, from the Dehalīvināyaka there,
in the east, tearing apart the elephants that are the heaps of powerful sins.
And I am Narasiṃha, who removes great fear, O great sage,
to the west of Pitāmaheśvara, terrifying to the fear of my devotees.
I am Atyugranarasiṃha to the west of Kalaśeśvara;
worshipped with faith, I remove even the fiercest flood of sins.
I am Jvālāmālīnṛsiṃha in the vicinity of Jvālāmukhī.
worshipped, I burn up the grasses that are the floods of sins.
I am Kolāhala-Nṛsiṃha, the crusher of Daityas and Dānavas;
for through the utterance of my name, the tumult of sin [ceases].
Where Kaṅkālabhairava is stationed, wise in protecting Kāśī,
worshipping me there with devotion, one is not obstructed by afflictions.
I am Viṭaṅkanarasiṃha, near Nīlakaṇṭheśvara;

4.61.s: tatra māṃ śraddhayā pūjya naro bhavati nirbhayaḥ ..97..
4.61.d: तत्र मां श्रद्धया पूज्य नरो भवति निर्भयः ..97..
4.61.m: worshipping me there with faith, a man becomes fearless.
And I am Anantavāmana, in the presence of Ananteśvara;
worshipped, I remove even endless taints of a devotee.
I am named Dadhivāmana, granting curd-rice to devotees;
by merely remembering whose name a man will never be poor.
I am Trivikrama in Kāśī, to the north of Trilocana;
worshipped, I bestow fortune and take away sins as well.
I am named Balivāmana, worshipped by Bali,
to the east of Balibhadreśvara, strengthening the strength of devotees.
To the south of Bhavatīrtha, come here from Tāmradvīpa,
I am named Tāmravarāha, granting what is desired to devotees.
O sage, [I am] Dharaṇīvarāha in the presence of Prayāgeśvara;

4.61.s: snātvā vārāhatīrthetra dṛṣṭvā māṃ kiṭi rūpiṇam ..3..
4.61.d: स्नात्वा वाराहतीर्थेत्र दृष्ट्वा मां किटि रूपिणम् ..3..
4.61.m: bathing here in the Vārāhatīrtha, seeing me in the form of a boar,
and worshipping [me] with abundant devotion, one would not enter the distress of a womb.
Giving even a little food there, one obtains the fruit of gifting the earth.
A person falling into the deep ocean of great sin,

4.61.s: mama bhaktyuḍupaṃ prāpya pralayepi na majjati .. 5 ..
4.61.d: मम भक्त्युडुपं प्राप्य प्रलयेपि न मज्जति .. 5 ..
4.61.m: attaining the raft of devotion to me, does not sink even at dissolution.
I am Kokāvarāha near Kiṭīśvara;
worshipping me there, a mortal obtains the desired fruit.

4.61.s: nārāyaṇāḥ śataṃ paṃca śataṃ ca jalaśāyinaḥ ..
4.61.d: नारायणाः शतं पंच शतं च जलशायिनः ..
4.61.m: Five hundred Nārāyaṇas, a hundred Jalalśāyins,
thirty tortoise forms, twenty fish forms,

4.61.s: gopālāśca śataṃ sāṣṭaṃ buddhāḥ saṃti sahasraśaḥ ..
4.61.d: गोपालाश्च शतं साष्टं बुद्धाः संति सहस्रशः ..
4.61.m: one hundred and eight Gopālas, Buddhas by the thousands,
thirty [Paraśu]rāmas, and one hundred and one Rāmas.
And I, as a single form of Viṣṇu, within the Muktimaṇḍapa,
am personally established, O sage, by the grace of Viśveśa.
In the form of Nārāyaṇa, the attendants, holding raised discs and maces,

4.61.s: kurvaṃti rakṣāṃ kṣetrasya parito niyutāni ṣaṭ .. 4.2.61.210 ..
4.61.d: कुर्वंति रक्षां क्षेत्रस्य परितो नियुतानि षट् .. 4.2.61.210 ..
4.61.m: six hundred thousand [in number], protect the sacred field on all sides.
Having heard this, Agnibindu, his bodily hairs bristling with joy,
the wise one asked again: 'O Lord, declare the different manifestations,
for the benefit of your devotees and for the pacification of my doubt.

4.61.s: kati te mūrtayonaṃta kathaṃ jñeyāstathā vada .. 12 ..
4.61.d: कति ते मूर्तयोनंत कथं ज्ञेयास्तथा वद .. 12 ..
4.61.m: How many are your forms, O Infinite One, and how are they to be known? Tell me that.'
Hearing this speech of Agnibindu, the storehouse of austerities,
Lord Viṣṇu explained the varieties of manifestations in sequence,

4.61.s: yāñśrutvāpi hi no martyo yamagocaratāṃ vrajet ..
4.61.d: याञ्श्रुत्वापि हि नो मर्त्यो यमगोचरतां व्रजेत् ..
4.61.m: having heard which indeed no mortal would go within the range of Yama.
The Lord of creatures stated the twenty-four varieties beginning with Keśava:
The blessed Viṣṇu said:
'O Agnibindu of great wisdom, listen, I shall tell you.
Know [them], O sage, starting from the upper right hand according to the order of creation.
Know the form of Keśava by the conch, disc, mace, and lotus,
which, when worshipped, beyond doubt accomplishes the desired aim of men.
Madhuhā is to be recognized by the conch, lotus, mace, and sword;
enemies perish through worship of that form.
Saṃkarṣaṇa is to be worshipped here, armed with conch, lotus, discus, and mace;
by worshipping that form, a creature will never be born again.
Dāmodara is worshipped with conch, Kaumodakī, disc, and lotus;

4.61.s: dadāti vittaṃ putrāṃśca godhanaṃ dhānyameva hi .. 19 ..
4.61.d: ददाति वित्तं पुत्रांश्च गोधनं धान्यमेव हि .. 19 ..
4.61.m: he indeed grants wealth, sons, cattle-wealth, and grain.
Vāmana is characterized by conch, disc, lotus, and mace;
even kept in the house, he makes a person wealthy.
[With] Pāñcajanya, mace, lotus, and the wondrous Sudarśana,
Pradyumna is worshipped by mortals; he bestows abundant wealth.
From the upper left hand, by creation, the group of six beginning with Viṣṇu is declared,
by mere remembrance of which masses of sin dissolve.

4.61.s: śaṃkhāribhyāṃ gadābjābhyāṃ pūjyo viṣṇuḥ śriye naraiḥ ..
4.61.d: शंखारिभ्यां गदाब्जाभ्यां पूज्यो विष्णुः श्रिये नरैः ..
4.61.m: Viṣṇu is to be worshipped by men for prosperity with conch, discus, mace, and lotus.
Mādhava, with conch, lotus, mace, and disc, bestows supreme prosperity.
Aniruddha should be meditated upon for complete success, bearing the conch, lotus, discus, and mace ready.
Puruṣottama is [worshiped] with the conch, mace, discus, and lotus.
Adhokṣaja, who removes rebirth, holds the conch, discus, lotus, and mace, O sage.
Janārdana is to be meditated upon with the conch, Kaumodakī, lotus, and discus.
Beginning from the lower left hand in clockwise order, the six forms beginning with Govinda [are described]:

4.61.s: śaṃkhaṃ cakraṃ gadāṃ padmaṃ goviṃdo bibhṛyātsadā .. 26 ..
4.61.d: शंखं चक्रं गदां पद्मं गोविंदो बिभृयात्सदा .. 26 ..
4.61.m: Govinda should always bear the conch, discus, mace, and lotus.
Trivikrama is to be worshipped with the conch, lotus, mace, and discus for prosperity.
Śrīdhara, bearing the conch, lotus, and discus, and holding the mace, [is worshipped] for prosperity.
Hṛṣīkeśa is recognized by the conch, mace, discus, and lotus.
Nṛsiṃha is considered [worshipped] with the conch and discus, lotus, and mace.

4.61.m: Then that sage, in the form of light, merged into the Kaustubha, the body of splendours,

Those whose minds are made bees at the lotus feet of Bindumādhava

One should always dwell in Kāśī, Bindumādhava should be seen,
this narrative should be heard, and the transmigration of the worlds should be conquered.
Holy is the origin of the Pañcanada; holy is the tale of Mādhava;

with all desires fulfilled, he shall become the lord of the fortune of liberation.

4.64.s: tena trailokyamakhilaṃ prīṇitaṃ tu mayā saha .. 3 ..
4.64.d: तेन त्रैलोक्यमखिलं प्रीणितं तु मया सह .. 3 ..
4.64.m: by him the entire three worlds, along with me, are pleased.
The virtuous person who pleases a man in the City of Liberation,
who abides there constantly for the ultimate goal of man, O brahmins, him I please.
Even Divodāsa, the royal seer, protecting Kāśī righteously,

4.64.s: sadeho matpadaṃ prāpto yato na punarāgatiḥ .. 5..
4.64.d: सदेहो मत्पदं प्राप्तो यतो न पुनरागतिः .. 5..
4.64.m: reached my abode in his own body, whence there is no return.
Here there is yoga, likewise knowledge, [and] liberation in a single birth;
therefore, having reached [A]vimukta, one should not go to another penance grove.
Knowing liberation to be very difficult to attain and transmigration very terrifying,
one should break one's feet with a stone and await time here.
When the foolish depart, abandoning Avimukta,
then the spirits will laugh, clapping their hands together.
Having attained holy Vārāṇasī, the peerless field of perfections,
what creature would have the thought to depart elsewhere?
And whatever fruit is obtained by men through a great gift elsewhere,
that is obtained in Avimukta when a single cowrie is given.
One might worship a liṅga, and another might perform austerity;

4.64.s: tayormadhye tu sa śreṣṭho yo liṃgaṃ pūjayediha .. 11 ..
4.64.d: तयोर्मध्ये तु स श्रेष्ठो यो लिंगं पूजयेदिह .. 11 ..
4.64.m: between the two, he is superior who worships a liṅga here.
Whoever duly gives a crore of cows at another sacred ford,
and whoever resides in Kāśī for a single day—of those two, the dweller in Kāśī is superior.

4.64.s: anyatra brāhmaṇānāṃ tu koṭiṃ saṃbhojya yatphalam..
4.64.d: अन्यत्र ब्राह्मणानां तु कोटिं संभोज्य यत्फलम्..
4.64.m: Whatever fruit [comes] from feeding a crore of brahmins elsewhere,
that is obtained in Vārāṇasī when even a single one is fed.
At the Sannihitī [pool] in Kurukṣetra, when the sun is seized by Rāhu,
giving alms in Kāśī is equal to the gift of a man weighed against gold. // 14
My supreme light is situated here, extending from Pātāla
beyond the seven worlds and so forth, boundless, assuming the form of a liṅga. // 15
Those who, even at the ends of the earth, remember my Avimukta liṅga,
are certainly freed from great defilements. // 16

4.64.s: asminkṣetre tu ye nāhaṃ dṛṣṭaḥ spṛṣṭaḥ samarcitaḥ ..
4.64.d: अस्मिन्क्षेत्रे तु ये नाहं दृष्टः स्पृष्टः समर्चितः ..
4.64.m: Whoever has seen me, touched me, and worshipped me in this sacred field,

4.64.s: saṃprāpya tārakaṃ jñānaṃ na sa bhūyobhijāyate .. 17 ..
4.64.d: संप्राप्य तारकं ज्ञानं न स भूयोभिजायते .. 17 ..
4.64.m: attains the saving knowledge and is not born again. // 17
He who, having worshipped me here, dies anywhere else,

4.64.s: janmāṃtarepi māṃ prāpya sa vimukto bhaviṣyati ..18..
4.64.d: जन्मांतरेपि मां प्राप्य स विमुक्तो भविष्यति ..18..
4.64.m: reaches me even in another life and will become liberated. // 18
Having thus spoken the greatness of the sacred field before the brahmins,
Hara vanished right there even as they were looking on. // 19
Having perceived Virūpākṣa directly before their eyes,
those brahmins, exceedingly delighted in mind, returned each to his own hermitage. // 4.2.64.120
Ascertaining the word of Śambhu, the omniscient treasure of compassion,
the brahmins cast aside other duties and worshipped only the liṅgas. // 21
Skanda said:
Having recited and caused others to recite this excellent secret narration,
a faithful person is freed from sins and is glorified in the world of Śiva. // 122

4.64.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśīti sāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ caturthe kāśīkhaṃḍa uttarārddhe kṣetrarahasyakathanaṃnāma catuḥṣaṣṭitamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 64 ..
4.64.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीति साहस्र्यां संहितायां चतुर्थे काशीखंड उत्तरार्द्धे क्षेत्ररहस्यकथनंनाम चतुःषष्टितमोऽध्यायः .. 64 ..
4.64.m: Thus ends the sixty-fourth chapter, entitled "Narration of the Secret of the Sacred Field," in the second half of the Kāśīkhaṇḍa, in the fourth [section] of the glorious Skandapurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses. // 64
